newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends weak on certification, long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends weak on certification, long bond.

text.p: Mexico peso contracts retained early weakness to straddle the key eight-per-dollar mark at the close of trade Thursday.

Traders said the U.S. House of Representatives vote on decertification of Mexico as an ally in the war on drugs and rising U.S. long bond yields hit the peso. "The market opted to trade on (U.S.) long bond movements and speculation triggered by the certification process," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended the session 3.5 and 2.7 centavos weaker, respectively, at 8.000/8.0050 and 7.9880/7.9930 per dollar.
The House of Representatives debate on decertifying Mexico's efforts to fight drug-trafficking was still under way when trading closed in Mexico's foreign exchange markets.
"The market was edgy and we feel the peso could slide further on Friday," another trader said.
Subsequently, the House voted to give Mexico 90 days to improve its performance in fighting the drug trade.

Yields on 30-year Treasury bonds were up to 6.98 percent when foreign exchange trading closed in Mexico, from 6.93 percent in early trade. Dealers said strong retail sales data triggered a sell-off in the U.S. bond market.
"I feel the market is still a little short (dollars), so that will stop the peso firming for a few days," a third trader said.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier 3.1 centavos weaker at 7.9810/7.9850 per dollar.
